title: Rabbi Yosta
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was a disciple of Resh Lakish. In [Yerushalmi Bava Metzia, chapter 10, halakhah 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Bava_Metzia.10.2): “Rabbi Yosta in the name of Resh Lakish: the lower owner provides the ceiling.” In the Bavli there, [117a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.117a), his name appears as Vestina, followed by “Resh Lakish said”; Dikdukei Soferim cites the variant Yostani. Shir HaShirim Rabbah gives “Rabbi Chunya in the name of Rabbi Yosta.” It appears that he is the Rabbi Yostina mentioned in [Bava Batra, chapter 8, halakhah 5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Bava_Batra.8.5), who had a case before the rabbis, was found liable, and appeared before Resh Lakish. At the beginning of Ketubot, chapter 9: “The rabbis of Rabbi Yostina asked R' Yochanan.”[^1][^2]

notes.text: The forms Yosta, Vestina, Yostani and Yostina remain reported variants; the identification is qualified by Hyman’s “it appears.” ר״ל, דק״ס and שהש״ר are rendered by the customary names Resh Lakish, Dikdukei Soferim and Shir HaShirim Rabbah. The abbreviated Bavli attribution is printed וסטינא אר״ל; its full unquoted teaching is not reconstructed. The Shir HaShirim Rabbah locator פ״ד פ״ח־ב corresponds to the checked passage at 4:8:2. רפ״ט means the beginning, not the end, of chapter 9. קם קומי is rendered “appeared before,” without adding an appeal outcome. בעו means asked, not entreated. The quoted passages were checked in the named digital editions; Dikdukei Soferim’s Yostani reading remains Hyman’s attribution.

The Guggenheimer Yerushalmi Bava Metzia passage explicitly names Rabbi Yosta reporting Resh Lakish; its Bava Batra case names Rabbi Yustinei appearing before Resh Lakish. These support the corresponding titles and the court-appearance wording, without independently proving discipleship or Hyman’s tentative identification. The checked [Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:8:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Shir_HaShirim_Rabbah.4.8.2) passage explicitly has Rabbi Chunya in the name of Rabbi Yosta. Davidson’s Bavli text has the form ו[יו]סטיני; Hyman’s Vestina and reported Yostani variant remain distinct. The retrieved Ketubot parallel has a different dialogue involving the rabbis of Rabbi Yostinei; it does not establish Hyman’s exact question to Yochanan, whose abbreviated title therefore remains R'.
